proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.targeted_by_spell
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing reaction trigger grammar can match a named spell, any spell cast with components, or a completed spell-save outcome, but not the generic case where a spell specifically targets the bearer and has no area of effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can take a Reaction to absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect"

proposed_widenings.name: absorb_triggering_spell_energy_into_charge_pool
proposed_widenings.justification: The current surface can negate a triggering spell and model a charge pool with an initial count and lifetime absorption cap, but it cannot add the triggering spell's level into the pool at reaction time while also enforcing the rod's lifetime absorption ceiling.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy-not the spell itself-is stored in the rod. The energy has the same level as the spell when it was cast. The rod can absorb and store up to 50 levels of energy over the course of its existence."

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_slot_substitution
proposed_widenings.justification: The current `grant_spell_access` atom only grants named spells. Rod of Absorption instead lets the bearer spend stored energy as a generic spell-slot substitute when casting their own prepared or known spells, capped by both the bearer's slot progression and a fixed item limit of level 5.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know. You can create spell slots only of a level equal to or lower than your own spell slots, up to a maximum of level 5."

notes: No authored Dhall/JSON/trace written. A composite magic-item family would be the right outer shape, but the reaction-side energy intake and the activation-side generic slot substitution are both missing from the current surface.
